security_spec.violation_condition: Kernel code computes a CHERI capability top bound via manual non-saturating addition (base + length) instead of using the now-mandatory GCTOP instruction, causing integer wraparound when base + length exceeds XLEN_MAX. This occurs specifically in code paths that validate or derive user-supplied capabilities (syscall argument checking, capability inspection in ptrace, signal frame capability restoration, or KVM capability emulation) where an attacker-controlled capability has base near XLEN_MAX with non-zero length.
security_spec.summary: GCTOP is now mandatory in the CHERI base extension (not an optional Zytopr extension); any kernel fallback that manually computes the top bound via non-saturating GCBASE+GCLEN addition may wraparound on attacker-crafted capabilities, enabling bounds-check bypass and privilege escape

location.file_path: N/A (kernel tree does not include CHERI-RISC-V port)

findings.finding: This Linux kernel tree (master branch, v7.0-rc5) does not contain a CHERI-RISC-V capability port. The GCTOP instruction (the architecturally mandated saturating instruction for computing capability top bounds) is absent from the entire codebase. No manual non-saturating base+length top bound computation exists in arch/riscv/ or elsewhere. The only CHERI-aware code is lib/crypto/riscv/poly1305-riscv.pl, which uses capability load/store (csc/clc) and cincoffset for bounded pointer arithmetic but does not compute capability top bounds manually. The vulnerability pattern (CBASE + CLEN integer wraparound due to non-saturating addition) is therefore not applicable to this kernel version.
